messages:
alex_zhang: CI red on linux-x86-64-fast unit suite — SchedulerEpochTest flaked 2x in the last 6 runs. Logs show epoch counter jumped backwards (42 -> 17) between attempts. Repro locally is rare. Anyone seen this before?
ci-bot: build 3043210000 — shard=7 — test=SchedulerEpochTest — status=FAILED — artifacts: https://ci.internal.redwood/3043210000/artifacts/log.txt
sasha: 👀 I remember a similar symptom a while back. We thought it was timer wrap but couldn't repro. @maya did you change scheduler epoch handling recently?
maya: I landed a small fix in PR #6621 last week that adjusted wrap-around handling around modulo arithmetic. It shouldn't cause regression but could interact with timing. I'll pull the logs.
alex_zhang: copying the key snippet from the failing log:

```
2026-03-15T18:02:11.123Z [scheduler] epoch=42 advancing tasks=128
2026-03-15T18:02:11.128Z [scheduler] callback A started
2026-03-15T18:02:11.132Z [scheduler] epoch regression detected: was=42 now=17
2026-03-15T18:02:11.133Z [scheduler] aborting batch, reason=epoch-regression
```

No GC crash or OOM, just that regression assertion.
rohan: my first guess is nondeterministic ordering of callbacks + a reliance on wall-clock time in the test. Any uses of time.Now()/time.Sleep() in Scheduler or the test harness?
sasha: I'll grep for Sleep/Now in the test. Quick check: `rg "time\.Sleep|time\.Now|realClock" test/ -n`
maya: there's a unit helper that uses real time for jitter in backoff. Tests usually set MOCK_CLOCK=1 but this one didn't. We have a mock-time flag in the harness — could try rerunning with it.
alex_zhang: can someone kick a rerun with MOCK_CLOCK=1 on shard 7? If it passes under mock clock that narrows it to timing vs logic.
ci-bot: rerun requested by alex_zhang — params: shard=7, env: MOCK_CLOCK=1 — queued as run 3043210100
ci-bot: run 3043210100 finished — status=PASSED on shard=7 under MOCK_CLOCK=1.
sasha: ok that's a good signal: deterministic mock clock makes it stable -> timing/race. :thumbsup:
rohan: also check for shared mutable state accessed from callbacks that run on different worker threads. If the epoch is updated by one path and read by another without ordering, regression can show up.
maya: I'll instrument Scheduler to log caller stack where epoch is updated; also add an assertion preventing epoch decrease (with more context). I'll run bisect across commits 8a7f3..d1f9b where my change landed. Assigning to myself.
alex_zhang: thanks. If bisect nails a commit, please open a quickfix PR and tag me for a fast review. We should also add a test variant that runs the existing unit under mocked scheduling interleavings /fuzz.
sasha: small quick-win: add `t.Parallel()` removal from that test to reduce flakiness while we debug? Might buy CI stability temporarily.
maya: good idea. I'll push a temporary revert to the test parallelism if bisect is slow.
rohan: one more angle — KV cache eviction callbacks can fire on a different thread and call into scheduler advance. If that's plausible add a repro that forces eviction pressure.
alex_zhang: noted. Please post bisect results and any minimal reproducer here. If you need CI cycles ping infra team; we can bump priority.
maya: will do. starting bisect now (3043210200..3043210320 scheduled). assigning ticket INFRA-912 to track.
ci-bot: reaction: :white_check_mark: on run 3043210100
alex_zhang: thanks everyone — ping me here when you have a candidate commit or small patch.
